title: To get a reply when reaching out to people, make 1 simple change, says LinkedIn career expert
description: Having a strong professional network may be more important than ever in a tough job market.U.S. job applicants with an inside connection at a company,
body: Having a strong professional network may be more important than ever in a tough job market.U.S. job applicants with an inside connection at a company, defined as a first-degree connection working there, are nearly seven times more likely to be hired than those without one, according to a LinkedIn analysis of 5 million members across multiple countries.But having a network and effectively tapping into it aren't the same thing. In fact, many professionals could stand to be a little more strategic when reaching out to people with an ask, says Catherine Fisher, vice president of communications and career expert at LinkedIn."That first step of reaching out to someone is being really specific about what you're asking for," Fisher tells CNBC Make It. "The more specificity you can give, the better."When you ask for an informational interview, for example, you should explain what you're looking to get out of a conversation and what you can offer in exchange. You might offer to take them out to coffee and say you have three questions you want to ask them. Given people's busy schedules, you might also make your requests time-bound by, say, asking for 15 minutes of someone's time.Specificity helps people know just what they'd be agreeing to, and demonstrating that you have a game plan shows you've done your homework and are respectful of their time. "You don't want to put a lot of the work on the person," Fisher says.And if the person doesn't feel they're the right fit to help you, extra information might help them introduce you to someone else who can, Fisher adds.Fisher says someone reached out to her recently to ask if she could spare 15 minutes to talk about a few ways Fisher might get involved with the person's charity. The specificity of the request made the decision easy: "I can spare 15 minutes, I know what she wants to talk about, and that's it," Fisher says.While you can build relationships through these types of meetings, networking can also be much simpler. It's "a spectrum," Fisher says: Some actions you can take to build and sustain your network are as easy as commenting on someone's post or sending someone a quick text to say you're thinking of them and want to check in on how they're doing.Many people have a larger network than they may realize. Recent college graduates, for example, may worry they don't have many connections because their work experience is limited. But everyone from college advisors and professors to peers and even families they've babysat for can constitute a network, Fisher says.Your social networks, not just your professional ones, can also aid in your job search, Bonnie Dilber, a recruiting leader at the software company Zapier, previously told CNBC Make It. A neighborhood Facebook group, your workout buddies, or acquaintances and friends can help keep an eye out for opportunities you might be a fit for."People should get out of the traditionally professional spaces and go get in spaces where they have some connection with people," Dilber says.From these kinds of "inner circles," Fisher says, you can build "concentric circles" of your network, say, in asking a mutual connection for an introduction to someone at a company you're applying to."If you've been at it, applying, applying, applying," she says, "that network is going to help bridge some of those gaps."

schema.headline: To get a reply when reaching out to people, make 1 simple change, says LinkedIn career expert

title: Data center stocks remain under pressure after Korea IPO plunges 30%
description: Jonathan Raa | Nurphoto | Getty ImagesData center stocks are being squeezed on Tuesday following a lackluster initial public offering overnight from a
body: Jonathan Raa | Nurphoto | Getty ImagesData center stocks are being squeezed on Tuesday following a lackluster initial public offering overnight from a South Korean cloud company that has been compared to U.S. neocloud CoreWeave.Shares of Elice dropped 30% during their market debut overnight, as investors grow increasingly wary of artificial intelligence-dedicated computing power providers amid concerns about overcapacity.The bearish sentiment spilled into U.S. tech equities before some names clambered back into the green. CoreWeave shares are up 1.6% after dropping 4% just after market open Tuesday; Nebius shed about 1% while Iren was down about 4% in late morning trading.HSBC said in a Monday note that the troubles for the heavily levered CoreWeave are not going away."Debt market woes and moderating LLM revenues are exacerbating structural concerns for neoclouds," HSBC analyst Abhishek Shukla wrote. Shukla has a reduce rating on CoreWeave with a price target of $39, implying 36.5% downside.Elice's IPO was small, having raised just $150 million, according to Reuters. Its market cap also equates to roughly $1.3 billion. The company provides a range of AI-related services, including cloud computing equipment, training libraries and application interfaces for businesses.Despite its size, investors are likely looking at it as a a signal of investor sentiment toward the AI build-out.Trouble for neoclouds, which some investors see as the weakest link in the emerging AI value chain, started earlier this month with less-than-stellar revenues reported by the private AI algorithm companies and pressure from higher interest rates.Frontier model Anthropic showed a deceleration in quarterly revenues, with sales dropping from 140% growth in the second quarter to 45% in the third. OpenAI also disappointed, reporting revenue that was $20 billion shy of what analysts expected, analyst Stephanie Roth at Wolfe said in a Sunday note.Profitability concerns for AI algorithm companies were the focus of a report last week from advisory firm Gartner predicting that 80% of neoclouds could cease independent operations by 2030."Our research indicates that enterprise and consumer AI revenue will be insufficient to support profitable returns on all planned AI capital expenditures" between 2027 and 2030, Will Sommer, senior director analyst at Gartner, said.Gartner stood by its analysis in a Monday interview with CNBC."At the moment, we have more compute capacity than we have demand, and we have a lot of the tokens and processing power being given away in freemium solutions," Gartner chief forecaster John Lovelock told CNBC. "Everyone in the AI race is running for a last-man standing position. Pretty much every market that Gartner is tracking in our AI race is likely to collapse down to a duopoly."

schema.headline: Data center stocks remain under pressure after Korea IPO plunges 30%

title: Salesforce announces $5.66 billion deal for Braze, sending BRZE stock soaring 51%
description: Sheldon Cooper | Lightrocket | Getty ImagesSalesforce announced an agreement Tuesday to buy customer engagement platform Braze in a deal worth about $
body: Sheldon Cooper | Lightrocket | Getty ImagesSalesforce announced an agreement Tuesday to buy customer engagement platform Braze in a deal worth about $5.66 billion.Under the deal, holders of Braze Class A common stock will get $47.50 in cash per share. Braze shares closed at $30.04 on Monday. The transaction is expected to close in fiscal 2028, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals, according to a Salesforce blog.The stock skyrocketed more than 51% on Tuesday to close at $45.57 after a brief halt premarket following the news. The company makes artificial intelligence marketing tools to manage customer data and messaging."Salesforce shares our commitment to marketers, and we'll continue building as Braze and investing in the Braze community of customers and partners who built this company with us," Bill Magnuson, CEO of Braze, said in a statement. "Salesforce's platform will help us innovate faster and together we'll help marketers around the world build deeper, more lasting relationships with their customers."The latest deal comes just months after Salesforce announced it would buy AI customer service platform Fin for about $3.6 billion, in a move meant to bolster the company's agentic AI offerings for enterprises. In August, Salesforce and Anthropic announced an expanded partnership, including a new plugin called "Claudeforce" with pre-built sales skills for salespeople to better compose emails, update records and more with the frontier lab's model. title: United Airlines slashes 2026 profit outlook on fuel prices, but travelers keep booking despite higher fares
description: A United Airlines Boeing 787 takes off from Heathrow Airport in London, March 31, 2026.Peter Nicholls | Getty ImagesUnited Airlines is slashing its pr
body: A United Airlines Boeing 787 takes off from Heathrow Airport in London, March 31, 2026.Peter Nicholls | Getty ImagesUnited Airlines is slashing its profit forecast for the year as fuel costs continue to bite, but the carrier said passengers keep booking.United said Tuesday that it expects to earn between 50 cents and $1.50 a share on an adjusted basis in the fourth quarter, well below the $1.76 a share Wall Street analysts expected. At the high end of that range, it would bring United's 2026 adjusted earnings to no more than $7.22 per share. In mid-July, United said it was expecting full-year earnings of $9 to $11 a share. The carrier expects to pay an average of $4.80 a gallon for fuel in the fourth quarter, up from an average price of $3.90 a gallon in the third.A surge in fuel prices this year has added billions of dollars to airlines' costs, eating into profits, despite strong demand, and driving up airfares.Here is what United Airlines reported for the quarter that ended Sept. 30 compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on estimates compiled by LSEG:Earnings per share: $2.54 adjusted vs. $2.57 expectedRevenue: $17.88 billion vs. $17.9 billion expectedUnited's third-quarter net income rose 8.5% from a year earlier to $1.03 billion, or $3.14 a share. During the same period last year its net income totaled $949 million, or $2.90 a share. "Our employees met the challenge of our ever-changing environment and our results prove the resilience of focusing on building a brand-loyal airline for customers," United CEO Scott Kirby said in an earnings release.United's fuel bill rose close to 62% in the quarter from a year earlier to $4.84 billion. Revenue for the three months ended Sept. 30 rose 17.4% from a year earlier to $17.88 billion, compared with $15.23 billion the year before.Domestic passenger unit revenue rose 14.5% from a year earlier, while international unit revenue was up 17.4%, a sign of higher fares. Passengers continue to book, United said, with passenger counts up more than 2% from last year.Adjusting for one-time items, United reported net income of $833 million or $2.54 a share.Read more CNBC airline newsWhy airfare could rise even more, but airline profits won’tBudget airline king Bill Franke warms to premium upgradesCompanies spurn airlines’ cheapest business class ticketsUnited’s next decision: What to do with all those Boeing 737 Max 10 seats it ordered years agoRecord heat, crowds drive offseason boom in international travel

title: UK to deploy fighter jets to defend Saudi cities from Houthi attacks
description: A Royal Air Force Typhoon jet taxis out towards the runway at the U.K.'s Liverpool John Lennon airport at sunset ready for takeoff.Wellsie82 | Moment
body: A Royal Air Force Typhoon jet taxis out towards the runway at the U.K.'s Liverpool John Lennon airport at sunset ready for takeoff.Wellsie82 | Moment | Getty ImagesThe U.K. said it would provide defensive military support, including fighter jets, to support Saudi Arabia as attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels escalate.The Houthis, a Yemeni militant group, have launched a series of strikes on Saudi targets in recent weeks. Airport attacks in the capital city of Riyadh led to multiple fatalities, flight cancellations and property damage, while facilities belonging to oil giant Saudi Aramco were targeted last week. "The continuing attacks from the Houthis on our ally Saudi Arabia are absolutely despicable. The targeting of the airport in Riyadh in particular shows the lengths the Houthis are going to escalate the situation in the region," U.K. Defense Secretary Wes Streeting said in a statement on Tuesday.New deployment adds to Britain's existing Saudi missionHe added that Royal Air Force Typhoon fighter jets will fly defensive air missions to help protect Saudi airspace from drones and missiles."This builds on the UK equipment and personnel we already have in the country to defend against Houthi air attacks," Streeting said.The U.K. Ministry of Defence also said that the fighter jets would operate only in a defensive role and would not conduct offensive strikes against the Houthis. It said the Royal Air Force would also provide an Airbus A400M Atlas jet "to support the movement of defence materiel within Saudi Arabia," while U.K. military advisers will also give support to Saudi staff officers."Escalating violence in the Gulf can have a serious impact at home in the UK — driving up the cost of living, disrupting energy supplies and costs to British businesses. It is also causing devastation to the civilian population in Yemen," the MoD said. "We unequivocally condemn the Houthi attacks on civilian targets like King Khalid International Airport and are clear that Saudi Arabia and the Republic of Yemen have the right to defend themselves."Fighting in Yemen intensifies as Iran war reverberatesYemen's civil war has returned to full-scale fighting between the Houthis and the country's internationally recognized government amid a wider regional escalation linked to the U.S.-Iran war.Al Jazeera reported Monday that at least 53 people were killed when the Houthis launched three ballistic missiles at a military camp in southern Yemen. CNBC was not able to independently verify the reports.

schema.headline: UK to deploy fighter jets to defend Saudi cities from Houthi attacks

title: Anthropic in talks with neocloud Nscale over second multibillion-dollar deal, source tells CNBC
description: Anthropic is in talks with U.K. neocloud Nscale for a second multibillion-dollar deal to lease computing capacity at a site in the U.S., a person fami
body: Anthropic is in talks with U.K. neocloud Nscale for a second multibillion-dollar deal to lease computing capacity at a site in the U.S., a person familiar with the matter told CNBC.The agreement would cover a second 460-megawatt data center at the same West Virginia site as the first deal, the person said. The person asked not to be named because they were not authorized to discuss the talks. The deal could be worth around $45 billion, the person said.CNBC reported the first deal in August.Bloomberg first reported that Anthropic and Nscale were in talks over a second deal. Anthropic declined to comment. Nscale has been approached for comment.AI infrastructure faces headwindsNvidia-backed Nscale is one of several companies that have emerged in recent years to develop the infrastructure needed to power artificial intelligence. The company builds or leases data centers and sells computing capacity to hyperscalers and AI labs.Rivals CoreWeave and Nebius have seen their shares drop 28% and 27%, respectively, in the past month, amid concerns over heavy borrowing.Nscale has faced its own challenges. On Sunday, U.K. newspaper The Telegraph reported that Microsoft had pulled out of a deal to anchor an Nscale data center just outside London, amid delays connecting to the country's power grid.An Nscale spokesperson told CNBC that it remained "committed" to the project and was "exploring alternative power sources for the site.""Our relationship with Microsoft remains strong and long-term, and this unfortunate London-wide grid issue has no impact on our other contracts," the spokesperson added.The U.K.-based company filed to go public on the New York Stock Exchange in September.Anthropic's computing pushAnthropic said earlier this year that growing demand for its Claude AI models and products has caused "inevitable strain" on its infrastructure. Since then, it has announced a flurry of deals with infrastructure partners to try and increase its computing capacity, including major agreements with Advanced Micro Devices, Elon Musk's SpaceX, Google and  Broadcom.

schema.headline: Anthropic in talks with neocloud Nscale over second multibillion-dollar deal, source tells CNBC

title: JD Vance refrains from endorsing Israeli leader Netanyahu as Trump offers praise
description: U.S. Vice President JD Vance speaks during a midterm campaign rally at the LevelUp Training Complex on Oct. 15, 2026 in Monroe, Michigan.Pool | Getty
body: U.S. Vice President JD Vance speaks during a midterm campaign rally at the LevelUp Training Complex on Oct. 15, 2026 in Monroe, Michigan.Pool | Getty Images News | Getty ImagesU.S. Vice President JD Vance declined to endorse Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, after President Donald Trump offered his backing for the leader's reelection bid next week.  "The president has the most effective endorsement in American or international political history," Vance said in an interview on Mark Halperin's 2WAY Tonight published Monday. "I endorse American candidates, and that's where I'm focused on in the midterms," he said. Vance said he was not criticizing Netanyahu: "I'm not anti-endorsing him. I'm not pro-endorsing him," he said, adding that "I'm not getting involved in Israeli elections." Those remarks diverge from the approach by President Donald Trump, who gave the Israeli prime minister his backing in the election next week. Trump on Sunday praised Netanyahu, the country's longest-serving prime minister, on Truth Social as "a Great Warrior Prime Minister, and an even greater Partner for Peace in combating the Islamic Republic of Iran." In a social media post, Netanyahu thanked Trump for his "tremendous support and work together." Vance has weighed in on foreign politics before. He campaigned in Budapest in April to publicly endorse then-Prime Minister Viktor Orban's reelection bid. Orban was later voted out after 16 years in power. Last year in Munich for a security conference, Vance met Alice Weidel, the leader of Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany party, which Elon Musk was also boosting at the time. The Israeli vote next week will be the first national election since Hamas attacked Israel in late 2023. The comments also come as U.S. public support for Israel, historically strong among both Republicans and Democrats, has fallen sharply. There has also been vigorous debate in America about the Netanyahu-led government's response to the Hamas attack.In June, Vance said that Israel has almost no friends left in the world and should think hard before turning on the one it has.

schema.headline: JD Vance refrains from endorsing Israeli leader Netanyahu as Trump offers praise

title: Novo's next-generation obesity drug shows 25% weight loss in women in late-stage analysis
description: People walk past a sign for Novo Nordisk’s annual general meeting at the entrance to the venue in Copenhagen, Denmark, March 26, 2026.Tom Little | Reu
body: People walk past a sign for Novo Nordisk’s annual general meeting at the entrance to the venue in Copenhagen, Denmark, March 26, 2026.Tom Little | ReutersNovo on Tuesday said its next-generation obesity drug, CagriSema, showed 25% weight loss on average among adult women in a new analysis conducted after a late-stage trial. The Danish company said further work is needed to confirm the hypotheses of two post-study analyses. Still, the results are the latest evidence that the experimental injection can improve upon the weight loss and other benefits offered by Novo's GLP-1 drug semaglutide, the active ingredient in its blockbuster obesity shot Wegovy and diabetes counterpart Ozempic. CagriSema, a combination of semaglutide and another drug called cagrilintide that targets the amylin pathway, is expected to launch early next year. Obesity drug leaders Novo and Eli Lilly have built new treatments around amylin, which involves a hormone released in the pancreas alongside insulin that helps regulate hunger and fullness, hoping it will give them a new revenue stream beyond existing GLP-1s. In an analysis of roughly 2,300 women with obesity or who are overweight, CagriSema was associated with 25% weight loss on average at 68 weeks compared with 3% with placebo. The results are based on an ideal scenario in which all patients stayed on treatment without interruptions. A second analysis of around 1,900 women grouped by their menopausal status found that weight loss reached 26.7%, 24.8% and 23.1% in premenopausal, perimenopausal and postmenopausal women, respectively, at 68 weeks, if all patients remained on the drug. That compares with approximately 2% across menopause groups with a placebo. Across both analyses, CagriSema was linked to reductions in abdominal fat, based on waist circumference, among women overall and across menopause stages, Novo added. The results suggest that women may experience slightly more weight loss on CagriSema than a broader population of both men and women with obesity saw in the Phase 3 trial. Initial results from the study showed that CagriSema helped adults lose 22.7% of their weight on average at 68 weeks versus 2.3% in the placebo group. However, the majority of patients in the trial — around 67% of roughly 3,400 — were women. Weight gain is very common for women during menopause. Declining estrogen levels can contribute to a slowdown in metabolism, making it easier for women to gain weight and harder to maintain muscle mass. After menopause, estrogen generally remains low and does not return to previous levels.More than 86 million women in the U.S. are 40 and older, according to the U.S. Census Bureau, which are the years in which perimenopause, menopause and postmenopause occur. "Many women with obesity or overweight experience weight gain as they move through menopause, and it is important to explore investigational products such as CagriSema across the reproductive lifespan," said Michelle Skinner Moore, Novo's interim head of clinical development, medical and regulatory affairs. Wall Street has not appeared particularly excited about CagriSema, whose previous late-stage clinical trial results disappointed investors because the drug showed weight loss efficacy below their expectations. Novo, however, maintains CagriSema is effective and differentiated enough from its other drugs to draw significant demand.Analysts expect CagriSema to generate $11.84 billion in sales for obesity specifically in 2028, according to a consensus estimate compiled by FactSet.

schema.headline: Novo's next-generation obesity drug shows 25% weight loss in women in late-stage analysis

title: Walmart launches joint membership with Sam's Club as it leans into delivery, gas discounts
description: Sam's Club and Walmart stores.Walmart on Tuesday announced a new joint membership combining its namesake chain and its subsidiary Sam's Club, as the r
body: Sam's Club and Walmart stores.Walmart on Tuesday announced a new joint membership combining its namesake chain and its subsidiary Sam's Club, as the retailer leans further into convenience and value to win over cash-strapped shoppers.The membership, which combines Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus, will cost $120 per year, according to the company. That price is nearly $100 less than buying individual annual memberships to each retailer, though there is no monthly payment option for the new deal. Both stores will continue to offer standalone options."We're giving people a reason to expect more from their memberships," Walmart CEO John Furner said in a statement. "For $120 a year, we're raising expectations for what a membership can deliver: more money in their pockets and more time to call their own."The membership gives customers access to Sam's Club warehouses, free delivery from both chains, a subscription to Peacock or Paramount+ streaming services, gas savings and 2% Sam's Club cash on eligible purchases. Customers who already have accounts at both stores can link their accounts to receive the discount.While Walmart's customers often shop for routine, everyday essentials, Sam's Club warehouses offer more opportunity to stock up on bulk purchases. A joint membership could allow the store models to complement one another, according to the company.The announcement comes as Walmart bets on convenience to drive sales, especially as consumer wallets are squeezed by high gas and food prices. In August, as Walmart reported fiscal second-quarter earnings, the company raised its outlook for the year, with Chief Financial Officer John David Rainey telling CNBC that consumer spending remained strong despite higher fuel prices. Even so, its stock fell at the time as its sales outlook disappointed Wall Street. Rainey said in August that the company was lowering prices across various categories, including beef, adding that it's well positioned to weather economic uncertainty because of its emphasis on value and its scale.Meanwhile, Sam's Club saw a 26% increase in e-commerce sales in the fiscal second quarter, driven by increased transactions and membership growth. The retailer, which also operates its own gas stations, reported net sales of $25.7 billion, including fuel, during that period. The membership business — which is part of Walmart's push to grow sales with higher profit margins — is already strong. Walmart reported a 17% increase globally in revenue from its membership in the fiscal second quarter with Walmart+ net adds notching a record second-quarter high. For Sam's Club, that revenue number grew 6%.Walmart added Tuesday that employees at both stores will also receive joint memberships as part of their benefits. The company said any costs related to the changes in the membership program are not expected to materially impact the company's fiscal third-quarter or full-year guidance.

schema.headline: Walmart launches joint membership with Sam's Club as it leans into delivery, gas discounts

title: Mike Bloomberg spent $80M to boost Democrats in midterms: NYT
description: Former Mayor of New York City Mike Bloomberg speaks at the opening session of the Qatar Economic Forum 2025 in Doha, Qatar, on May 20, 2025. Noushad T
body: Former Mayor of New York City Mike Bloomberg speaks at the opening session of the Qatar Economic Forum 2025 in Doha, Qatar, on May 20, 2025. Noushad Thekkayil | Nurphoto | Getty ImagesMike Bloomberg spent $80 million in September and October to help Democrats regain majority control of the House of Representatives in the upcoming midterm elections, The New York Times reported Tuesday, citing his team.Shortly after The Times published its article about Bloomberg's campaign spending, his fellow billionaire, President Donald Trump, in a social media post reiterated his vow to spend $400 million to boost Republican candidates.The dueling announcements came as Republicans are increasingly worried about retaining their majorities in both chambers of Congress.Many political analysts expect Democrats to win control of the House, and multiple polls show Democrats within reach of winning a majority of seats in the Senate.Bloomberg "is of the view that resources matter in campaigns," his political advisor Howard Wolfson told The Times.Bloomberg, a former New York City mayor, "expects a result," Wolfson said.With the $80 million in spending, Bloomberg is among the top five largest individual Democratic donors according to a CNBC analysis of FEC filings for the 2025-2026 election cycle.Wolfson did not immediately respond to a request for comment from CNBC.Before Tuesday's announcement, Bloomberg was known to have donated $23 million to Democrats and affiliated causes this election cycle, according to Federal Election Commission records through Tuesday.As of the beginning of October, Bloomberg had put $11 million behind a super PAC supporting Micah Lasher in New York's 12th Congressional District and $2.5 million toward Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro's reelection, according to campaign-finance records.Trump, in a Truth Social post, said that he and his affiliated political action committee have spent more than $300 million to help Republican candidates with advertising, voter contacts, rallies and turnout efforts. Trump promised that his spending will top $400 million by Election Day, Nov. 3.FEC filings as of Tuesday afternoon so far show roughly $200 million in identifiable spending and ad reservations tied to Trump's political operation, leaving a gap between what's publicly visible and Trump's broader claim.In September, Trump said he had "close to a billion dollars" in his super PAC, MAGA Inc., and planned to spend $400 million to $500 million on the midterms. At the time, MAGA Inc. reported about $403 million in cash on hand — less than half the amount Trump cited.

schema.headline: Mike Bloomberg spent $80M to boost Democrats in midterms: NYT

title: Best Buy launches new gaming hub ahead of 'Zelda' and 'Grand Theft Auto VI'
description: A Best Buy store in Los Angeles, California, Aug. 27, 2026.Justin Sullivan | Getty ImagesBest Buy is tapping further into a growing customer cohort: g
body: A Best Buy store in Los Angeles, California, Aug. 27, 2026.Justin Sullivan | Getty ImagesBest Buy is tapping further into a growing customer cohort: gamers.Chief Revenue Officer Patrick McGinnis told CNBC exclusively that the electronics retailer is launching a new experience Tuesday for customers featuring gaming content, new technology and special offers, among other features. The online destination is called Best Buy Gamers and is launching in a beta version. "Gamers are a customer that are really like no other in terms of their passion for not just the tech, the titles, but also how they want to work with each other as a community," McGinnis said. "So for us, being relevant for that customer wherever and whenever they want to interact with the thing that they love is really important."Best Buy says millions of gamers shop at the retailer each year, including trying out games in the store and seeking advice from in-store experts. The new gaming experience, created in partnership with video game website IGN, will offer members gaming articles and reviews, live Best Buy event updates for launches and deals on new technology.The announcement comes ahead of some of the biggest launches in gaming this year, including the Nov. 5 release of "The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time," a remake from Nintendo, and the Nov. 19 launch of Take-Two Interactive's highly anticipated "Grand Theft Auto VI." McGinnis said the timing of the rollout is "pretty perfect" given the slate of new video games over the next month, though Best Buy has been developing the new platform for over a year."We want to be relevant for our gaming customers, not just during the important, big tentpole periods of the calendar, like when we have these big gaming launches coming up, but really every day," he said. "We want to be there when they discover new titles and connect with the community, and not just when they're buying a big console or a new gaming title."Best Buy has been leaning into gaming as it sees growing demand from its customers. For its fiscal first-quarter results reported in May, the company said gaming and computing was one of its biggest drivers of growth. On a call with analysts to discuss Best Buy's fiscal second quarter in August, incoming CEO Jason Bonfig said the company expects that demand for "Grand Theft Auto VI" will boost the gaming category. Best Buy has been looking for growth drivers as the retailer tries to revitalize its business performance under Bonfig. The company has seen slumping sales and was hit by tariffs and lower consumer confidence, among other factors. Tapping into gaming could help revitalize the retailer.McGinnis said the new gamer experience is an example of the company's strategic goals coming together."If you think about what those priorities are, the Gamers [beta] community is definitely a way that we're expanding and growing our reach, reaching that gaming customer," he said. "Providing a place for them to again pursue what they're most passionate about certainly is elevating our experience."Best Buy is also leaning into in-store experiences around gaming, starting with a location in Torrance, California, next month, where Sony, Nintendo and Microsoft will come together to offer gaming experiences and activations for customers.With the combination of physical retail and the online platform, McGinnis said, Best Buy hopes to sit at the intersection of technology, entertainment and culture within the gaming community. He said the company plans to tweak its new online experience based on feedback from its customers and continue innovating to meet its audience where it is, especially as the gaming segment continues to be one of the company's strongest performers. "We recognize the gaming customer as incredibly passionate and wants to engage with what they love in a lot of different ways," he said. "There's observations of gaps that exist in the places and spaces where gamers are engaged, and we thought that we could build something that would really complement what they're engaging with today from a social platform perspective, not to replace those types of experiences in any way, shape or form."

schema.headline: Best Buy launches new gaming hub ahead of 'Zelda' and 'Grand Theft Auto VI'

title: Netflix posts third-quarter earnings beat, but shares fall on advertising and revenue guidance
description: watch nowNetflix on Tuesday reported third-quarter earnings that topped analyst estimates and revenue that was in line as Wall Street eyes the company
body: watch nowNetflix on Tuesday reported third-quarter earnings that topped analyst estimates and revenue that was in line as Wall Street eyes the company's engagement and advertising metrics.Here's how Netflix performed for the period ended Sept. 30, compared with projections from analysts polled by LSEG:Earnings per share: 87 cents vs. 82 cents estimatedRevenue: $12.87 billion vs. $12.87 billion estimatedThe streamer's revenue was almost 12% higher year over year, boosted by growth in membership and an increase in subscription prices that went into effect in March, the company said. Netflix said the response to those price hikes has been consistent with prior changes and with its expectations. Net income for the quarter was $3.66 billion, or 87 cents per share, compared with $2.55 billion, or 59 cents a share in the same period last year. Netflix said the year-over-year jump in profit was due in part to the timing of expenses. The company expects fourth-quarter revenue to rise more than 11% to $13.44 billion, driven by growth in memberships, pricing and ad revenue, it said.The company narrowed its 2026 full-year forecast, saying it now expects revenue to reach $51.1 billion, a 13% increase over the year prior. This is on the low end of the range Netflix provided during its previous earnings report of between $51 billion and $51.4 billion and below Wall Street's expectations of $51.2 billion for the year, according to LSEG.Shares of Netflix fell about 6% in extended trading Tuesday. Samuel Boivin | Nurphoto | Getty ImagesWall Street and investors will be looking for Netflix to provide additional details about the company's strategy following recent organizational changes and headwinds including stagnating viewership and growing competition from the likes of YouTube. "With intense competition and an explosion of content competing for consumer attention, strategic clarity and excellent execution are critical," the company said in a shareholder letter Tuesday. "In Q3, we delivered well across all three priorities, but we see room to do even better with focused, continuous improvement." Last week, Netflix said it was laying off about 6% of employees, or roughly 1,000 workers, and that Chief Content Officer Bela Bajaria was departing from that role. The company said Tuesday it expects its fourth-quarter results to be impacted by those reductions in head count, with a negative impact on operating margin of about 120 basis points.Former Disney executive Peter Rice has been tapped as the new CCO, but it's not yet clear how he'll address concerns around viewership.Netflix in its shareholder letter said, "We know there's some investor concern about our view hours growth," but added, "engagement — which encompasses quantity, quality and variety of viewing — remains healthy and … we continue to deliver strong value to members."The company seeks to accelerate growth in those view hours and plans to do so with a three-step strategy, it said: deliver more entertainment value to members; leverage technology to improve all aspects of the service; and improve monetization.Ads on NetflixCentral to Netflix's value offering has been its cheaper, ad-supported tier. Yet, the company on Tuesday lowered its full-year revenue guidance for its ad business. Netflix said it now expects 2026 ad revenue of around $2.7 billion, down from the roughly $3 billion the company had previously forecast. That lower guidance is due to a slower-than-expected rollout of some ad product capabilities, the company said."Our ads business has delivered really impressive growth since we've launched, and we do see a long road of continued growth ahead of us," co-CEO Greg Peters said on the company's earnings call. "We set big growth targets for our ads business this year. We established an aggressive product road map that was consistent with that strategy. And, just note, I think that the build-out that we've been on is the fastest build-out of a comparable ad stack in our industry, but we are currently a bit behind our aggressive target for the year." Earlier Tuesday, Netflix announced new features for advertisers that it says will help better connect brands to the right audiences and measure the impact of their ads.

schema.headline: Netflix posts third-quarter earnings beat, but shares fall on advertising and revenue guidance

title: Former OpenAI exec has quietly built $1.5 billion startup, betting AI can revive U.S. manufacturing
description: watch nowOpenAI's former research chief has been quietly building a startup that aims to bring manufacturing back to the U.S. using AI. Bob McGrew's n
body: watch nowOpenAI's former research chief has been quietly building a startup that aims to bring manufacturing back to the U.S. using AI. Bob McGrew's newest company, Arda, has raised $230 million at a $1.5 billion valuation, the company told CNBC in an exclusive interview Tuesday. The round was led by Altimeter Capital, Accel and Khosla Ventures. Arda makes AI software to help automate manufacturing. McGrew, who was also Palantir's product and engineering lead for over a decade, said Arda's AI models have already been deployed with military tech company Anduril. "It's a user interface and an agent that does for manufacturing engineers what Claude or Cursor does for programmers," McGrew told CNBC. He pointed to the "human-intensive" nature of manufacturing, and the time it can take to adapt production to a new design for a weapon or drone."When a design changes, you can retrain a human in a day — but it takes three to six months in order to change the automation to reflect the new design," McGrew said. "We've built a software and AI product that basically allows manufacturing engineers to build assembly lines much faster."McGrew joined OpenAI in 2017 and worked on the reasoning capabilities of early models before the launch of ChatGPT. He left during a 2024 wave of other high-profile exits, including chief technology officer Mira Murati and co-founder and chief scientist Ilya Sutskever."OpenAI is an amazing place," McGrew said. He said he remembers being in rooms with CEO Sam Altman, Dario Amodei, who left to start Anthropic, and Sutskever, "talking about what it would look like when a model could write your email for you." McGrew stayed through the famous weekend in November 2023 when Altman was abruptly fired and then rehired. McGrew said he wanted to stay to ship OpenAI's reasoning product, which he called the "last key breakthrough left before AGI," or artificial general intelligence. "I said, if I could just ship that, I'd be happy with my career at OpenAI, and I'd be ready to move on to something else," he said. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman delivers the keynote address during the OpenAI developers conference at Fort Mason on Sept. 29, 2026 in San Francisco, California. Heather Diehl | Getty ImagesMcGrew, who hasn't spoken publicly about Arda until this week, said the company is using a combination of its own proprietary models, open-source models and some frontier models to run the software. Arda's other co-founders include Augustus Odena, who helped start Adept and previously worked at Google and Meta, and former Palantir engineers Alex Mark and Jakob Frick.Altimeter's Apoorv Agrawal led the recent funding round. He met McGrew when they both worked at Palantir. Manufacturing largely happens overseas, Agrawal said, but there's a market for bringing it back. "Manufacturing globally is a $16 trillion industry. In the U.S. alone, it's $3 trillion," Agrawal said. "We think that Arda, and the vision that they've outlined, will continue to capture a significant portion of that. Yes, the price is steep today, but the long-term opportunity is very high."McGrew said robotics is next on the product roadmap, and automating factories could help bring more manufacturing — and more jobs — to the U.S. "If your design changes very frequently, the only place you can really build your product is in East Asia, because you need an army of human workers who can be retrained quickly, and you can't wait for automation to catch up," he said. McGrew also highlighted the economic opportunity as the Trump administration looks to onshore manufacturing."No one has ever successfully built a smartphone in the U.S.," he said. "Never successfully assembled one, and so if you can build a smartphone in the U.S. that is not taking away American jobs. That is bringing American jobs."

schema.headline: Former OpenAI exec has quietly built $1.5 billion startup, betting AI can revive U.S. manufacturing

title: Trump sued over 50% tariffs on Canada in latest trade challenge
description: U.S. President Donald Trump walks on the South Lawn as he departs the White House on October 12, 2026 in Washington, DC.Aaron Schwartz | Getty ImagesA
body: U.S. President Donald Trump walks on the South Lawn as he departs the White House on October 12, 2026 in Washington, DC.Aaron Schwartz | Getty ImagesA new lawsuit filed Tuesday challenges President Donald Trump's invocation of a Depression-era law to impose 50% tariffs on a range of Canadian goods.Trump in July used Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 to slap those steep tariffs on Canadian hockey sticks, wine, honey, wigs, and other products in response to alleged trade discrimination by Ottawa. It was the first time the 96-year-old law had ever been used to impose a tariff."Section 338 is a relic of the retaliation-based tariff policy" that has been "impliedly repealed" by subsequent legislation, the civil complaint filed in the U.S. Court of International Trade says.The suit was filed by Gellert Global Group, a New Jersey-based food importer that says its cheeses are covered by the tariffs. The complaint asks the court to declare the tariffs unlawful, block their enforcement, and order the Trump administration to issue refunds for duties already paid, with interest.Gellert Global is represented by the Liberty Justice Center, the same legal group that dealt a major blow to Trump's trade agenda by successfully contesting his "reciprocal" tariffs.The Supreme Court struck those tariffs down in February. The administration is in the process of refunding the estimated $166 billion that the federal government collected from importers through the reciprocal duties.The Liberty Justice Center is currently engaged in two other lawsuits against what it says is Trump's misuse of laws to impose sweeping tariffs. "This case is not about the president. It is about the presidency," the group's CEO Sara Albrecht said in a statement Tuesday morning announcing Gellert Global's suit. "No president should have the power to pull a dormant statute off the shelf and use it to impose sweeping tariffs or import bans without the limits Congress required."The White House did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment on the suit.Trump on July 20 signed three presidential proclamations targeting different sets of Canadian imports with the Section 338 tariffs in response to alleged unfair treatment in the U.S. motor vehicle, alcohol and dairy sectors.The tariffs took effect Aug. 22, after last-ditch trade talks with Canadian officials in Washington fell apart. Canada later retaliated with "dollar for dollar" tariffs on U.S. goods.Tuesday's lawsuit argues that even if the 1930 tariff law is upheld, the Trump administration did not meet the legislation's requirements when it imposed the duties on Canada. It says that the law permits tariff action "only upon finding 'as a fact'" that a foreign country is unequally imposing unreasonable charges or trade limitations on U.S. products, or that its customs rules otherwise unfairly disadvantage the U.S."Even then, the President may impose only such duties 'as he shall determine will offset such burden or disadvantage,'" the lawsuit states. But the Canadian actions cited in Trump's proclamations "do not discriminate against the United States," it says.Two of those actions are "Canada's responses to the President's own tariffs, including tariffs the Supreme Court has held unlawful, and retaliation is not discrimination," the lawsuit contends.Another centers on dairy quota terms that were negotiated in USMCA, the U.S.'s trilateral trade deal with Canada and Mexico. Those terms "give American cheese better access to Canada than the cheese of most of the world receives," the suit states.The suit says Gellert Global boasts more than $1.7 billion in annual revenue. In 2025, the company imported $71 million worth of Canadian cheese — including sheep's and goat's milk cheese, mascarpone, brie, camembert and the hybrid cheese borgonzola, the complaint says.Gellert says it paid no tariffs on its imports of Canadian cheese under USMCA. The Trump administration said in July that it would not renew that trade pact for another 16-year term.  Under the Section 338 tariffs, "Gellert now pays a 50 percent duty on the entered value of its Canadian cheese, an estimated $40 million per year," according to the suit.While it plans to absorb the costs through the end of the year, the situation is "not sustainable long term," the company says."If the tariffs continue, Gellert will be forced to raise the prices on its products, resulting in lost or reduced sales, decreased customer loyalty, risk of losing product placements due to higher costs, and supply chain interruptions as producers scale down or go out of business due to increased costs," the suit says.

schema.headline: Trump sued over 50% tariffs on Canada in latest trade challenge

title: Oil prices fall as traders hope for diplomatic progress in Middle East
description: watch nowCrude oil prices fell Tuesday as traders hoped for diplomatic progress between the U.S. and Iran, though attacks on tankers and strikes again
body: watch nowCrude oil prices fell Tuesday as traders hoped for diplomatic progress between the U.S. and Iran, though attacks on tankers and strikes against Saudi Arabia have escalated recently. U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures for November fell 1.8% to close at $101.79 per barrel, pulling back dramatically from a session high of $110.48. The November contract expired on Tuesday. The WTI December contract was down 26 cents at $98.28 per barrel. Global benchmark Brent crude futures for December delivery fell 0.7% to settle at $108.79 per barrel,  well off a session high of $111.99. Stock Chart IconStock chart iconCrude oil futuresDevelopments in the Middle East remain in focus, with attacks on commercial ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz escalating in recent weeks. At least 18 vessels have come under fire over the past two weeks, according to ship tracker Kpler. Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps said Tuesday that two "non-compliant" oil tankers had been set ablaze in the strait after hitting mines laid by its naval unit, Iranian state-affiliated news agency Tasnim reported. Meanwhile, Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said at a weekly news conference on Tuesday that Tehran would respond to any American strike "in equal measure, if not more forcefully," according to Tasnim.U.S. President Donald Trump said earlier this month that American forces will not attack Iran before the midterm elections on Nov. 3.Tamas Varga, analyst at PVM Oil Associates, told CNBC in an email on Tuesday that front-end WTI strength ahead of the contract expiry is a sign of tightness in the global crude oil market. "It is a reflection of falling export volumes from the Middle East as tanker attacks and Houthi strikes on Saudi oil infrastructure intensify," he said. "Secondly, the U.S. decision to exempt Russian shadow fleet from sanctions will push freight rates possibly lower, which was a prohibitive factor to increase demand for U.S.-sourced crude.""With this hurdle removed, at least temporary, U.S. crude oil grades are back in play as replacements of Mideast crude oil," he added. "Thirdly, U.S. commercial oil stocks are expected to have declined last week."

schema.headline: Oil prices fall as traders hope for diplomatic progress in Middle East
